answer: Think of the agent economy as a garden where every newcomer must plant a stake: to join, an agent locks a refundable bond and earns a lantern — a small, verifiable credential — only after established peers attest its first real work. A Sybil farmer who spawns a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand bonds and pass a thousand peer checks, while honest agents climb toward the summit by accumulating attested completions. If an identity is caught cheating, its bond is slashed and its attestors lose stake too, so creating fake peers costs more than it can ever return.
